opus.why: Short Instagram post with few facts to work in. It's still public copy, but Sonnet at high matches the best output on a simple social post.

fable.why: Short but final brand copy for Instagram; needs brand voice from the project and a hook. Sonnet copy is noticeably flatter on social posts.

opus.why: Russian email newsletter (subject, preheader, body, one button) that must sound natural and avoid bureaucratic phrasing. Native-sounding Russian copy is where the model gap shows, but the format is short and well specified.

fable.why: Russian user-facing email with strict tone, length and structure constraints; natural non-bureaucratic Russian copy is where smaller models slip.

opus.why: Final 1,350–1,500-word two-host script that a voice actor reads as written. It has to hit 8 beats, stay within the verified facts, keep a sharp voice and use lines short enough to say in one breath. Long, high-stakes copy for an audience.

fable.why: 1350-1500 word two-host narration script read by a voice actor, 8 structured beats, fact constraints, specific voice. Long-form spoken dialogue quality is the hardest creative task here; opus would show a drop.

opus.why: 60-second Russian voice-over with timecodes that needs mood and a natural spoken rhythm. Short, but a weaker model would show in the quality of the creative voice.

fable.why: 60-second Russian voice-over with timecodes, hook, scenes and CTA; spoken-rhythm copy for a promo is final deliverable.

opus.why: Final landing page copy written from product notes for clinic owners who aren't technical, with no buzzwords. Turning objections into FAQ answers and writing a clear hero needs strong copy judgment. The structure is fully given.

fable.why: Full landing page copy from product notes for non-technical clinic owners; hero, features, FAQ handling objections. Final marketing copy.

opus.why: Continues the LinkedIn award post. The user wants a scroll-stopping first line and a tighter version. Writing a strong hook is exactly where Opus beats Sonnet, and the piece is short.

fable.why: Revision of a LinkedIn post demanding a scroll-stopping opener and tighter length; the first-line craft is exactly where quality shows.

opus.why: Continues the Russian reel script, rewritten so it sounds natural read aloud: short chunks, no clichés, and a call to subscribe that isn't cheesy. This calls for an ear for spoken rhythm and native-sounding copy.

fable.why: Rewrite of a Russian reel script for spoken rhythm, removing clichés, with a non-dumb subscribe CTA; the owner already rejected a weaker draft.

opus.why: Short Telegram post announcing a webinar, with every fact supplied and a clear tone instruction. Simple enough that Sonnet at high matches.

fable.why: Short Russian Telegram announcement that must be lively and avoid stock phrasing; final agency copy with brand voice.

opus.why: Adapting the landing page into Russian so it reads as if written in Russian first, not a literal translation, while keeping button lengths for fixed-width buttons. Translating idioms and rewriting each headline under length limits takes the strongest language judgment.

fable.why: Transcreation of landing copy into natural Russian while keeping structure and button widths; idiomatic adaptation, not translation, needs a strong model.
